article.title: Tua Tagovailoa Named Falcons Starting Quarterback for Week 1
article.summary: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. (AP) — Tua Tagovailoa has been named the Atlanta Falcons’ starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the team announced Monday. The decision comes after Tagovailoa’s monthslong competition with Michael Penix Jr., wh...
article.content_html:
Key Developments

The Atlanta Falcons have officially named Tua Tagovailoa as their starting quarterback for the upcoming Week 1 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. This decision concludes a lengthy competition between Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., who had previously started nine games for the Falcons in the 2025 season before sustaining a season-ending torn ACL in November.

Coach Kevin Stefanski announced that Cooper Rush will serve as the backup quarterback to Tagovailoa, while Penix Jr. will be inactive for the season opener. Stefanski declined to comment on the team's starting quarterback plans beyond Week 1.

Throughout training camp, Tagovailoa received more valuable practice repetitions than Penix Jr. Although Penix Jr. was cleared for 11-on-11 drills on August 22, he did not participate in any preseason games for the Falcons. Stefanski acknowledged Penix Jr.'s recent return to full practice, stating, "Of course, Mike just getting back to 11-on-11, wanted to make sure we gave him an opportunity in these practices, and we did. But feel strongly about our decision with everything, all the information available to us."

Tagovailoa played in both the first and final preseason games for the Falcons. In his final exhibition game against his former team, the Miami Dolphins, he completed 7 of 8 passes for 95 yards over three drives. He orchestrated an 8-play, 60-yard touchdown drive on Atlanta's opening possession but also lost a fumble on his second drive. The Falcons ultimately won that preseason game against the Dolphins, 17-12.

Stefanski expressed pride in his entire quarterback room, which includes Tagovailoa, Penix Jr., Rush, and undrafted rookie Jack Strand. "Really, really proud of those guys," Stefanski said. "Those guys have worked like crazy all offseason, and they’ve pushed each other, supported each other, and that’s what we’ll do for Tua. We’ll continue to support him and understand that this is a collective group that is constantly looking to help each other."

Tagovailoa joined the Falcons on a one-year deal in March, following a six-year tenure with the Miami Dolphins. Miami remains responsible for $99.2 million over the next two seasons due to a four-year, $212.5 million contract extension awarded to Tagovailoa in 2024.

Key Takeaways

  • Tua Tagovailoa has been named the starting quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons' Week 1 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
  • Michael Penix Jr., who previously started for the Falcons, will be inactive for the season opener, with Cooper Rush as the backup.
  • Tagovailoa received more practice reps during training camp and played in two preseason games, including a strong showing against his former team, the Miami Dolphins.

Why It Matters

The decision to name Tua Tagovailoa the starting quarterback marks a significant step for the Atlanta Falcons as they aim to establish a stable and effective offense. Tagovailoa's experience, including his previous success with the Dolphins, brings a known quantity to the Falcons' signal-caller position. The move also highlights the team's confidence in Tagovailoa's ability to lead the offense, especially after Penix Jr.'s injury last season. The inactive status of Penix Jr. suggests a longer-term plan for his return and integration, while Cooper Rush's role as backup provides experienced depth. This quarterback situation will be closely watched as the Falcons navigate the upcoming season, with Tagovailoa's performance being crucial to the team's success.
